\section[la fidanzata]{la fidanzata — a girlfriend, a fiancée}

\label{lesson:IT-C164-fidanzata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for a worker, then the Italian for an office worker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la fidanzata}
\textbf{la fidanzata} — \textquotedblleft{}a girlfriend, a fiancée\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{fidanzata} is \textquotedblleft{}the one pledged\textquotedblright{}: from \emph{fidanzare}, \textquotedblleft{}to betroth\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{fidanza}, \textquotedblleft{}trust\textquotedblright{}, which goes back to Latin \emph{fidere}, \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB 2.1 lists French \emph{fiancée} as its cognate.
\end{cousinweb}
